137	Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
138	The API issues a single access token that is valid for one week and has no refresh endpoint. A client that needs a new token logs in again.
139	Invented for this demo.
140	Reason: Security review SR-2025-14 of the pilot found that a stored refresh token let a stolen browser profile keep access for months. The team chose a one-week access token and no refresh token, so a stolen token expires on its own. Invented for this demo.

143	
144	Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.
145	Deleting an article or a comment runs a SQL DELETE. No deleted_at column exists.
146	Invented for this demo.
147	Reason: Legal review LR-77 requires that content its author deleted is gone from live storage within 24 hours. A deleted_at column was rejected because the rows would stay in the table. Invented for this demo.
148	
149	## reset-link-lifetime
150	
151	Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
152	The API has no password reset flow yet. This fixes the rule for when it is built: a reset link works once and expires 30 minutes after it is sent.
153	Invented for this demo.
154	Reason: Support tickets showed that users open a reset mail within 10 minutes. A link that lives 30 minutes covers slow mail delivery without leaving a long-lived link in an inbox. Invented for this demo.
155	
156	## reject-fancyhash
157	
158	The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.
159	Password hashing stays on passlib with bcrypt. The fancyhash package was evaluated and rejected.
160	Invented for this demo.
161	Reason: The licence of fancyhash has a network-use clause that is not compatible with distributing the API. Passlib with bcrypt was kept. Invented for this demo.
162

164	
165	bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
166	No custom rounds value is set on the password context, so passlib's default applies.
167	Invented for this demo.
168	Reason: Load test LT-9 put the login endpoint at a p95 of 240 ms with the default factor. One step higher pushed it past the 300 ms login budget. Invented for this demo.
169	
170	## page-size-default-reason
171	
172	The article list defaults to 20 items per page.
173	The default limit of the article list is 20 items.
174	Invented for this demo.
175	Reason: Design review DR-31 found that the mobile list screen fits 20 rows without scrolling. Invented for this demo.
176	
177	## favorites-no-notification
178	
179	Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.
180	Adding a favorite writes a database row and nothing else. No message is sent to the author.
181	Invented for this demo.
182	Reason: Product decision PD-8 puts all notifications out of scope until the 2027 roadmap. Invented for this demo.
183	
184	## postgres-over-mongodb
185	
186	PostgreSQL is the data store and MongoDB was not chosen.
187	Articles, tags and favorites are stored in PostgreSQL tables joined by foreign keys.
188	Invented for this demo.
189	Reason: The data is relational, and the DBA team supports only PostgreSQL (ADR-3). Invented for this demo.
190	
191	## aiosql-over-orm
192	
193	Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.
194	Every query lives in a SQL file that the repositories call by name.
195	Invented for this demo.
196	Reason: The DBA team reviews every query. A SQL file can be reviewed in a pull request and ORM output cannot (ADR-4). Invented for this demo.
197	
198	## tokens-header-only
199	
200	Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
201	The API reads the token from the Authorization header. It does not set or read any cookie.
202	Invented for this demo.
203	Reason: Cookie transport would need CSRF protection that this API does not have (ADR-5). Invented for this demo.
